c1_dinner.direction: Single antique copper kitchen sieve with a small tied bundle of dried rosemary behind it, seen close from below, hanging vertically from a short dark cord at the top center. Warm low amber evening practical in a Californian family restaurant; a honey-colored rim on the left and deep warm shadows elsewhere. The entire artwork is just the hanging object, no extensions, no room, no typography. It will hang at the far upper right over the existing room.

c3_archive.direction: A narrowly cropped deep-shadow side of a stack of two worn mahogany archival index drawers, closed and unmarked, viewed from near floor height three-quarters from its right. Flecks of honey-colored light catch the two brass drawer pulls. Low contrast, purposeful silhouette, simple, old and believable. This is a nearest-camera foreground layer at the very far lower left beside stacks, never a collectable or puzzle.

c8_beach.direction: A single irregular small clump of wind-bent coastal marram grass, brown-green waxy blades with just a few pale fragile straw seed heads angled to the left in the wind, against complete transparency. View from close to the wet ground. Naturally overcast cold slate afternoon on the Pacific shore. The root tangle is underneath the lower edge, no rock or earth around it. Elegant dark silhouette with faint silver light.

c9_gallery.direction: Alien architectural cornice fragment of translucent dark Baltic amber and honey-glass, with a single slender iridescent luminous capillary thread. The organic graceful curving rib descends diagonally from upper right toward bottom left, like a converging branch, tapering away to a delicate free end; displaced soft amber light from beneath. A clip of the closest upper-left vaulting in an alien sleeping gallery. Just this one architectural component on transparency, no room or lit background.
